claim:
`Pre Filter 1 - 2 - 6` at `40 03 03` and `Post Filter 1 - 2 - 6` at `40 03 05` sit on one type, one on each side of its degrader, and are printed with the same name ending over the same range and the same six byte values. **They are two tables.**

**What the pre filter holds is a gain ladder with one stage switched across it.** Five of its six entries are three rungs 5.99 dB apart, and the rungs are gains rather than shapes: over the bands this reads they are the same number in every band to within 0.53 dB, against 0.62 dB from the same six entries swept twice in two sessions, and they tilt by 0.04 dB per octave at worst over six of them. The odd entries carry one stage and the even entries carry it with something else added, and the something else is the same curve both times: the step from entry one to entry two and the step from entry three to entry four agree to 0.16 dB at the median and 0.69 dB at worst. Entry nought is not a fourth rung: it stands 17.13 dB under entry one with a spread of 1.76 dB and a tilt of -0.27 dB per octave, both outside what the floor produces, so it is a different shape and not the bottom of the ladder.

**And what that stage is, is a notch and not a low pass.** It falls to -8.20 dB at 8000 Hz and comes back to nothing above it, reaching a quarter of a decibel of flat again by fifteen kilohertz -- which a corner cannot do and a dip in the middle of the band can. Fitted as a second order notch with its centre, its sharpness and its depth all free, the centre lands at 8000 Hz (Q 0.42, 0.61 of the way to a full null, residual 0.146 dB), and moving the centre five hundred hertz either way more than doubles that residual. **8000 Hz is a quarter of 32000 Hz**, which is the clock this archive reads on classes that share no takes with these -- a delay ladder, a degrader's own two nulls -- and which nothing in this fit was told.

**What the post filter holds is not that.** The same three rungs, asked the same way, are shapes and not gains: they spread 2.90 to 2.96 dB where the pre filter's spread 0.31 to 0.53. The same alternation is there and its stage agrees with itself just as well (0.20 dB), but it is a different stage: deepest at 132 Hz where the pre filter's is deepest at 8000 Hz, with nothing below it coming back, and the two differ from each other by 5.28 dB at the median against a floor of 0.15. The entry that passes the most is the last of one byte and the first of the other.

**So a rule closed on one of them does not reach the other**, and the two are indistinguishable to anything reading the printed page: same last word, same range, same hex values, same type.
named: A gain ladder with a notch switched across it, and a shelf table -- two tables under one printed name.
why_not_named: The pre filter's own name is what this contradicts, so it is not reused. Five of its six entries move level and one fixed curve in and out, and the curve is a dip at a quarter of the clock rather than anything with a corner. Whether the dip is one tap added at two samples or a second order section is an open reading below.

measurements.why: The pre filter at all six of its entries, with the degrader at the entry the claim on that byte measured to be the flat one and the post filter at the entry this record measures to pass the most. The held block is the whole of what makes these six profiles comparable.
The same six entries under the same held block in a second session. This is the floor every figure in this claim stands on, and it is a floor over six settings rather than over repeats of one.
The post filter at all six entries with the pre filter shut.
The same six entries with the pre filter at the entry that passes the most instead of the least, which is what says the post filter's table does not depend on what is handed to it.

document_rows.why: What the page prints for the two, which is what makes them one signature to a reader and to the estimator that decides what a closed claim reaches. The page states a range and a count and says nothing about what an entry is.

era_priors.prior: A part of this period implements a cheap fixed colouration as taps on a delay line it already has, rather than as a section with coefficients, because the taps cost an add and the section costs a multiply per sample per order.
era_priors.would_be_wrong_if: The dip sat at a frequency that is not the clock over twice a whole number -- which is every frequency but a handful, and is where the freely fitted centre was free to go. It would also be wrong if the dip's flanks were narrower or wider than a tap's cosine allows at the depth measured, which is the reading the standing alternative below names and which this claim has not made.
era_priors.why: It is why one tap at a whole number of samples is a candidate here at all, and it is not why the dip is where it is. Where it is, is measured, and the prior is beaten on the residual by the section it argues against.

adds: The two bytes had no claim on them and neither had ever been read, though the takes for both have been published since the degrader beside them was closed. What is new is the structure inside each table -- a ladder with a switch for one, a shelf table for the other -- and the measurement that they are not one table.

floor.from: the pre filter swept twice under one held block in two sessions

the_pre_filters_ladder.read_as: Two of the three rungs are the same six decibels from twenty four hertz to eight kilohertz, which is nine octaves and is what answers a reading that has the entries differing only outside the bands. The third does not: it is the rung that climbs off the loudest entry and it reads twelve decibels below sixty three hertz where it reads six everywhere else. Something at that entry puts energy under the rung, which a floor cannot do because a floor is added to both ends of a rung and makes it read small. What it is is not read here.

the_stage_the_even_entries_switch_in.read_as: The section wins on the residual and it has three free parameters to the tap's one, so the residual is not what is read out of this. What is read out is where the free centre went: it went to a quarter of the clock, which is the one frequency the tap could have put it at and is not a frequency the fit was given. A section placed there by its own fit and a tap that cannot be placed anywhere else are two accounts of one measurement, and which of them the part holds is open below.
the_stage_the_even_entries_switch_in.not_rendered_through_the_band_set: Both candidates are read at the band centres and the unit is read as band energies, which is the comparison this project has measured to matter on a narrow feature. The dip here is an octave wide at half its depth, so the correction is small -- but it is not zero and it is not made, and the residual difference between the two candidates is the size where it could matter. That is the reason the choice between them is left open rather than the reason it is made.

the_post_filters_table.read_as: No rung is a gain and every one of them spreads about five times what the pre filter's widest does. The first entry is the open one and the five above it take the bottom of the band out, which is what a table of band limiting shelves looks like and is not what a ladder looks like. The alternation is there and the stage it switches is a different stage: it deepens toward the bottom and nothing below it comes back.

the_post_filter_does_not_depend_on_what_.what: Its six entries were swept twice, once with the pre filter at the entry that passes the least and once at the entry that passes the most -- twenty nine decibels of level, through a degrader, into the byte being read.
the_post_filter_does_not_depend_on_what_.read_as: Over the bands this reads, the six profiles agree between the two sessions to between 0.14 and 0.19 dB, which is inside the floor. Below a hundred and twenty five hertz they do not, by four to sixteen decibels, and the same table says why: at the shut setting the five attenuating entries sit under eight decibels over the silence down there and at the open one they sit over thirty three. The bottom of the band is where this reading runs out and the record's own silence profile is what says so.

the_two_are_not_one_table.the_ladders: the pre filter's is a gain and the post filter's is not
the_two_are_not_one_table.read_as: Three separate ways, none of which needs the other. The rungs: gains on one byte and shapes on the other, five and a half times apart in spread. The stage that alternates: a dip at eight kilohertz against a shelf deepest at a hundred and thirty hertz, five decibels apart at the median against a floor of a sixth of one. And the index: the entry that passes the most is the last of one and the first of the other, which is a fact about the table and not about anything downstream of it.

alternatives.reading: The two bytes are one table read at two places in the chain, and what tells them apart is the degrader between them rather than the table.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: Which entry of a table passes the most is a property of the index and nothing downstream reorders an index. The pre filter's open entry is its last and the post filter's is its first, and no stage sitting between two reads of one table can reverse which way the table runs. The stages the even entries switch in are different stages by five decibels at the median against a floor of a sixth of one, and one of them returns to flat above its dip while the other does not return at all.

separated_by.observable: The post filter's six profiles with the level in front of it moved by twenty nine decibels.
separated_by.answered: They agree to between a seventh and a fifth of a decibel over the bands this reads, which is inside the floor.

alternatives.reading: The stage the pre filter's even entries switch in is one tap added at two samples, rather than a second order section placed at the same frequency.

separated_by.observable: The shape of the dip's flanks against frequency, read against both candidates rendered through the same band set the unit was read on.

predicts.one tap: A cosine in the frequency, so the flanks are fixed once the depth is: nothing about their width is free.
predicts.a section: Flanks whose width is set by a sharpness that has nothing to do with the depth.

separated_by.sensitivity_here: The two stand 0.187 dB apart in residual on the reading made here, and the reading made here is the one that has not been rendered through the band set.
separated_by.why_not_separable: Not by a run, and the run is not what it wants. Both candidates are already fitted on published takes and what separates them is an arithmetic this reading did not do: rendering each through the band energies the unit was read as, rather than sampling it at the band centres. This project has measured that correction to decide a comparison on a narrow feature and has not measured it on one an octave wide. Until it is made, the smaller residual is not a reason to prefer the section, and the tap's inability to put its dip anywhere but where the dip is, is not a reason to prefer the tap.

alternatives.reading: The pre filter's rungs are six filters that differ only outside the bands this reads, and the six decibels is their passband gain.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: Two of the three rungs are the same six decibels from twenty four hertz to eight kilohertz, which is nine octaves and is most of what this unit puts out. A filter differing outside that has almost nowhere left to differ in. It is not ruled out above eight kilohertz on the third rung, which is where the reading stops and says so.

separated_by.observable: The same three rungs read in the two octaves below the band set this claim's other figures are read over.

predicts.six filters: The rungs are not six decibels there.

separated_by.answered: Two of the three are 5.79 to 6.03 decibels in all three regions. The third is 5.91 where this reads and 12.09 below sixty three hertz, and that one is not ruled out.

could_have_been_refuted_by: Six entries whose differences were six unrelated curves; a step between two entries that tilted; the step from entry one to entry two disagreeing with the step from entry three to entry four; a free notch centre landing anywhere but on a simple fraction of the clock; the post filter's profiles moving when the level in front of it moved by twenty nine decibels; or the two bytes returning the same table, which is what the printed page and the estimator both expect.
refuted_by: A reading of either byte on a second unit of this model returning a different number of rungs, a different step, or the dip at a frequency that is not a quarter of this clock.
what_it_would_change: A renderer of this type needs two tables and not one, and needs to know that the pre filter's entries are mostly a drive into the degrader rather than a band limit -- which is what decides how much the degrader distorts at each of them. It also fixes the one entry a renderer cannot take from the others: the first, which is not on the ladder.
what_this_does_not_settle:
What entry nought of the pre filter is. It stands seventeen decibels under entry one with a shape the floor does not account for, and the bands where that shape lives are the bands where whatever the type leaves behind is loudest, so this reading can say it is not a fourth rung and cannot say what it is instead.

What is at the top of the third rung. That rung reads twice its size below sixty three hertz, at the loudest entry of the table and nowhere else, and neither the cause nor whether it reaches the bands this claim's figures are read over is established.

Whether the dip is a tap or a section, which is the standing alternative above.

Whether the same two tables are on the second Lo-Fi type. `01 73` prints a `Lo-Fi Type 1 - 2 - 6` over the same six byte values and has no record of it at all, and the two bytes read here being two tables is the reason not to assume it is a third copy of either.
